title: 2014 HMMT November Theme Problem 7
statement: Let \(\mathcal{P}\) be a parabola with focus \(F\) and directrix \(\ell\). A line through \(F\) intersects \(\mathcal{P}\) at two points \(A\) and \(B\). Let \(D\) and \(C\) be the feet of the altitudes from \(A\) and \(B\) onto \(\ell\), respectively. Given that \(A B=20\) and \(C D=14\), compute the area of \(A B C D\).

solutions.text: 140 Observe that \(A D+B C=A F+F B=20\), and that \(A B C D\) is a trapezoid with height \(B C=14\). Hence the answer is \(\frac{1}{2}(A D+B C)(14)=140\).
